clue.text: Accommodation allowance including fare originally between New York and LA

indicators.note: including says the allowance word holds the rest inside it

parts.note: a grant is a sum allowed or awarded

indicators.note: between puts one letter in the gap separating the two city abbreviations

parts.note: LA is the abbreviation for Los Angeles

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word fare

explanation.surface: A housing benefit stretched to cover an initial flight fare from New York to Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'allowance' looks like part of the definition but is wordplay; the definition is just 'Accommodation', a self-contained annexe.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-contained annexe for an elderly relative is a kind of living accommodation.

clue.text: Doctors covering area must get breaks

indicators.note: covering says the doctors' letters wrap round the area letter

parts.note: GPs are general practitioners, family doctors

explanation.surface: Physicians who cover a district are owed time off.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaks as nouns are openings or intervals, which is what gaps are.

clue.text: Order the majority of tropical fruit

indicators.note: order as a verb means arrange, so the letters are put in a new sequence
the majority of means most of the word, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: Asking for most of the exotic fruit on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the majority of' trims TROPICAL to TROPICA; 'Order' rearranges those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The apricot is a small orange stone fruit.

clue.text: Citizen bound to be heard in charitable organisation

parts.note: a national is a citizen of a country

indicators.note: to be heard says the tied-up word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: bound means tied up, trussed

explanation.surface: A citizen obliged to speak up within a charity.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer names a large British charity that looks after historic houses, gardens and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: This British heritage body is a registered charity, so it is a charitable organisation.

clue.text: Searched around at home, exhausted

indicators.note: around says the search word goes round the home word

parts.note: fished, as in fished about for something, means searched
in means at home

explanation.surface: Worn out after rummaging about the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausted and used up are synonyms for being done with, all spent.

clue.text: Something cast in gold for so long

indicators.note: in says the cast object sits inside the gold symbol

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a die is something cast, as in a throw of dice

explanation.surface: A golden object made in a mould that lasts for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something cast' reads like a metal casting but means a die thrown in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: So long is an informal farewell, the same as the French goodbye.

clue.text: Film on European saga

indicators.note: in a across clue on means the film piece is attached after the European letter

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film

explanation.surface: A movie about a European saga.
explanation.definitionFit: A long heroic tale is both a saga and an epic.

clue.text: Bag taken from here in Naples turned up

indicators.note: turned up says the hidden letters are read backwards
taken from says the letters are lifted out of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bag snatched in Naples has turned up again.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Bag taken' as the definition, but 'taken from' is the signal that the letters are lifted from 'here in Naples'; the definition is just 'Bag'. In a down clue 'turned up' reads them upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A pannier is a bag, especially one slung on a bicycle or a pack animal.

clue.text: Conservative lists delayed new start

parts.note: a ship that lists leans to one side
late means delayed

explanation.surface: A Conservative has put back the publication of lists, wanting a fresh beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lists' looks like a noun but is a verb: leans, as a ship does.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiping the board clean is an idiom for a fresh beginning.

clue.text: Moralistic type managed to protect Italian after backing up

indicators.note: after says the protected piece comes behind the turned word
backing means the little word up is turned round

parts.note: the word up taken as written before being turned

indicators.note: to protect says the managed word surrounds the Italian abbreviation

parts.note: ran a business means managed it
IT is short for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: A prudish person who had to shield an Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: A Puritan is someone with strict moral views who disapproves of pleasure.

clue.text: Have an effect, seeing Gemini, unusually, welcoming power

indicators.note: welcoming says the jumbled sign takes the power letter inside
unusually says the star sign's letters are set out in an unusual order

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: An astrology reading where Gemini oddly gains power and makes an impact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges GEMINI into IMINGE, and 'welcoming' takes P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear upon or encroach on something is to have an effect on it.

clue.text: Millions up, USA lost for being faint-hearted

indicators.note: lost means all at sea, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A timid American market: millions gained, then the money is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking courage or resolve; cowardly and timid.

clue.text: Go over before quiet son gets mixed grill

indicators.note: before says the crossing word comes first

parts.note: to cross is to go over

indicators.note: gets mixed says the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cook visits the mixed grill station before a silent son arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grill' seems to belong with 'mixed' as food; it is the definition, meaning interrogate.
explanation.definitionFit: To grill someone is to interrogate them closely, questioning a witness already examined.

clue.text: Rumour of European objective for border crossing?

indicators.note: rumour suggests something passed by word of mouth, so the European is taken by sound

parts.note: a Czech is a European, from the Czech Republic
the point of something is its objective

explanation.surface: A whispered report about a European goal at a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarded post on a frontier where travellers are inspected; the question mark marks it as an example.

clue.text: Trouble that comes at bath time?

definitions.meaning: being in trouble is an idiom, a difficult or awkward situation
the hot tap runs at bath time, read literally

explanation.surface: Bath time brings tears and a squabble.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for trouble, and literally what fills a bath.

clue.text: Test on fluid sort of arrangement

indicators.note: in an across clue on puts the test after the fluid abbreviation

parts.note: FL is the abbreviation for fluid, as in fl oz
an oral is a spoken test or exam

explanation.surface: An exam on liquids, organised in some way.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower display is a kind of arrangement, described with this adjective.

clue.text: Old newspaper article about name for plant

indicators.note: about says the article goes round the name letter

parts.note: a leader is a newspaper's editorial article

explanation.surface: An old newspaper piece discussing what to call a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleander is a poisonous evergreen shrub with pink or white flowers.

clue.text: Badly wants company checks

parts.note: to vet a candidate is to check them

explanation.surface: A firm that screens applicants desperately wants something.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn greedily for what belongs to someone else is to want it badly.

clue.text: 6-0 — fast and furious

parts.note: 6 in Roman numerals is VI and 0 looks like the letter O
Lent is the Christian fast before Easter

explanation.surface: A rapid, angry 6-0 scoreline, like a tennis set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' reads as quick but is the noun: the Lenten fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Furious can mean wild and forceful, as in a raging storm.

clue.text: Nice reshuffle of seat plan

indicators.note: a reshuffle rearranges, so the letters of the two words change places

explanation.surface: A dinner-party host redoing the seating plan in Nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' at the start, capitalised, suggests the French city; it means agreeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreeable and enjoyable; a synonym for nice.

clue.text: Medical condition of drivers around unstable mines

indicators.note: around says the drivers' letters go round the rest

parts.note: the AA, the Automobile Association, is a British motoring organisation for drivers

indicators.note: unstable says the letters of the word are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Drivers near collapsing mine workings suffer a medical problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drivers' stands for Britain's Automobile Association, a motoring club; 'unstable' jumbles the five letters it surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of memory is a recognised medical condition.

clue.text: Delivery panic to ruin mobile working

indicators.note: mobile means moving freely, so the letters move into a new order

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A broken-down mobile phone causing panic over a delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: A speaker's delivery is the way words are spoken, their articulation.

clue.text: Carbon charge for old banger

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: A carbon levy on an old car.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for an old, battered car (also a sausage).
explanation.definitionFit: Crate is slang for a decrepit old car or aircraft.

clue.text: Ravel's measure of pace

definitions.meaning: to ravel is to tangle or entwine
a nautical speed unit, one nautical mile per hour

explanation.surface: The composer Ravel's tempo marking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ravel's' suggests the composer; it is 'Ravel is', the verb meaning tangle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangle in thread, and the unit of a ship's speed.

clue.text: Reluctance to move home — age holds it back

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: holds says the age word contains the turned piece

parts.note: an era is an age

indicators.note: back means the word it is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Someone loath to move house because of advancing age holding them back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IT into TI, which ERA holds, giving ERTIA.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics and everyday use, resistance to any change of state or motion.

clue.text: Give up evil calls

parts.note: to drop a habit is to give it up
sin is wickedness, evil

explanation.surface: A preacher urging the congregation to renounce wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Visits informally, pays a casual call on someone.

clue.text: Children may be shot small

definitions.meaning: small measures of spirit, shots, drunk in one go

explanation.surface: A sinister line about youngsters being shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Young children, and small drams of spirits.

clue.text: Downer of French worker packing iron

indicators.note: packing says the first pieces are stuffed with the iron word

parts.note: de is French for of
a worker ant, the stock crossword worker
to press clothes is to iron them

explanation.surface: A French labourer carrying an iron, feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: A downer is slang for a sedative drug that lowers mood or activity.
